64.content:
Zara Larsson didn’t just drop an album, she set the digital stage ablaze. Her latest project, Midnight Sun, has stormed onto charts around the world, proving yet again that Sweden’s brightest pop export knows how to command the global spotlight.

**A Streaming Tsunami**
-----------------------

In its first full day of release, Midnight Sun racked up an eye-watering 3,872,952 million streams on Spotify. That number secures it as Zara’s second-best debut album on the platform, behind her blockbuster 2017 effort So Good with 9.45 million streams. For perspective: her last two projects, VENUS and Poster Girl, clocked in at 2.75M and 2.71M, respectively.

That’s not growth, it’s an explosion.

**Entering the global leagues**
-------------------------------

The princess of Swedish pop is also world royalty. Zara made history and entered Spotify’s Top Artists Global for the first time ever, arriving at #177 as the largest new entry. Back on her home turf of Sweden, though, she’s a complete behemoth: Zara ascended 30 positions to claim the #1 spot on Spotify Sweden’s Daily Top Artists. And if you ever doubted it, she’s sat on Sweden’s Top Artists list for a staggering 1,437 days in a row, or nearly four years straight without budging.

Sweden Just Can’t Stop Playing Midnight Sun

All of the songs from Midnight Sun entered Sweden’s Top 100 simultaneously, a not-so-common achievement reserved for a few of the world’s major pop titans. The best bits:

#3. “Blue Moon” – 118,282 streams (New)  
#12. “Hot & Sexy” – 79,927 streams (New)  
#16. “Midnight Sun” – 69,777 streams (+10)  
#41. “Crush” – 41,237 streams (Re-entry)  
#44. “The Ambition” – 40,379 streams (New)  
#52. “Girl’s Girl” – 36,555 streams (New)  
#55. “Eurosummer” – 35,680 streams (New)  
#85. “Pretty Ugly” – 29,631 streams (Re-entry)  
#88. “Puss Puss” – 29,138 streams (New)  
#98. “Saturn’s Return” – (New)

That’s not a debut, it’s a complete sweep.

**Critics Are Eating It Up**
----------------------------

And if the numbers weren’t proof enough, Zara also earned her best reviews to date. Midnight Sun launched with a sparkling 89 on Metacritic, a whopping best rating for the album so far. For comparison: VENUS had a 74, Poster Girl had 72, and her first So Good had a 76. With Midnight Sun, Zara isn’t just racking up streams, she’s long deservingly receiving the critical flowers.

**Apple Music and iTunes Dominate**
-----------------------------------

The hot streak doesn’t end on Spotify. On Apple Music, Midnight Sun charts in the top 10 in 27 nations, 8 of them in the top 5. Standouts include:

*   #1 Sweden
    
*   #2 Kuwait
    
*   #3 Brazil
    
*   #3 Netherlands
    
*   #4 Norway
    
*   #4. Saudi Arabia
    
*   #4 Serbia
    
*   #5 Portugal
    

On iTunes alone, the album made a big impact in the United States, opening at #41, and also going to #1 in Sweden and to the top of 20 charts in Brazil, Turkey, Canada, Thailand, and the United Kingdom.

Album Review: Zara Larsson – Midnight Sun
=========================================

2 min read

![Image 2](https://renownedforsound.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/Zara-Larsson-2023.jpg)

Zara Larsson’s rise from teenage Swedish talent show winner to global pop star was driven by bold ambition – and _Midnight Sun_ is meant to be no exception. Written during a rare break from touring, much of the album took shape on late-night writing retreats in the Swedish countryside, where Larsson says she rediscovered the joy of making music purely for herself. Released via Epic Records, it’s her fifth studio album and one that looks to reflect a more introspective, playful side of the singer. In an album that is meant to be packed with personal reflections, so let’s see how that translates into the audio…

![Image 3](https://renownedforsound.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Zara-Larsson-%E2%80%93-Midnight-Sun.jpg)Kicking off with title track _Midnight Sun_, and, for me, it’s her strongest offering – a poppy plucky drum and bass hi-hat and bass, using the consecutive 24-hour periods of sunlight that the Swede no doubt experienced in her homeland. _Blue Moon_ continues the plucky instrumentation, this time the track was a bit more chart house, while the beginning of _Pretty Ugly_ started with shouting (a la _Hollaback Girl_), and _Girl’s Girl_ feels a little slower in tempo, and to be honest, a bit dated – at this point it starts to feel a bit samey.

_Crush_ up next – clearly one of the better tracks… better instrumentation and a better hook, but as per the previous tracks it does somewhat lack in substance. Sadly, _Eurosummer_ returns to giving me 15 year old euro pop vibes, which maybe is the point of the track, while both _Hot & Sexy_ and _The Ambition_ definitely continued the late 2000’s/early 2010’s kind of vibe.  Penultimate track _Saturn’s Return_ stood out for being different – a slower tempo, and honestly that alone made it one of the better tracks on the album, whilst _Puss Puss_ definitely gave me Kei$ha vibes.

I think it’s obvious that I wasn’t a huge fan of _Midnight Sun_, the production and instrumentation felt dated and a bit tinny, whilst the whole vague/random dance beats with lyrics over the top didn’t do it for me, all felt like an album lacking in real substance and quality. I don’t love giving negative reviews, and to be fair, if I was reviewing an EP of _Midnight Sun_, _Crush_ and _Saturn’s Return_, I’d say it wasn’t really for me, but nonetheless decent/good tracks, but the otherwise “Midnight Sun” as an album was not up to scratch for a seasoned artist – thumbs down from me (sorry Zara).
